one_liner: Go package of AVX2/NEON assembly kernels for and/or/xor/andnot/not, any-bit and popcount over []byte; beats Go loops 5-20x.
what_it_does: Bulk bitwise operations on Go byte slices: And, Or, Xor, AndNot, Not and Memset write into a caller-supplied dst; Any and AnyMasked report whether any bit (of a, or of a&b) is set; Popcnt and PopcntMasked count set bits. It is a plain function API (package name `and`) with no allocation; the two-input functions panic when slice lengths differ. There is no stdlib equivalent except crypto/subtle.XORBytes for the xor case.
how_it_is_fast: The Go gc compiler does not auto-vectorize, so a byte or uint64 loop runs scalar; go-and replaces the bulk of each slice with unrolled SIMD loops (eight 32-byte VMOVDQU/VPAND-style ops per 256-byte block on AVX2, a 128-bit AVX1 variant, sixteen 16-byte NEON registers per 256-byte block on arm64) and finishes the tail with a uint64 Go loop. Any/AnyMasked use VPTEST with an early exit; amd64 Popcnt is an 8-way unrolled scalar POPCNTQ loop and arm64 Popcnt uses NEON CNT with byte-lane adds and UADDLV. CPU features are picked at run time via golang.org/x/sys/cpu, or at compile time with GOAMD64=v2/v3; the amd64 assembly is generated by avo (internal/asm/src.go), the arm64 assembly is hand-written.
when_to_use: Go code doing bitmap/bitset algebra on byte slices of a few hundred bytes or more: bloom filters, roaring-style dense containers, posting-list bitmaps, image masks.
Hot loops that intersect two bitmaps and only need to know whether the intersection is non-empty (AnyMasked) or its cardinality (PopcntMasked), without materialising the result.
amd64 servers with AVX2 (Haswell and later) or Apple Silicon / other arm64 where the NEON And/Or/Xor/AndNot/Popcnt paths exist.
Cache-resident working sets (the measured 80+ GiB/s rows use 32,000-byte buffers); this is where SIMD beats a scalar Go loop by the largest margin.
when_not_to_use: Slices under 256 bytes: the SIMD loops only run on whole 256-byte blocks for and/or/xor/andnot/not/any (128-byte with AVX1), so short slices fall through to the uint64 Go loop plus a non-inlinable call.

XOR only: Go's own crypto/subtle.XORBytes is already assembly (16-byte SSE2 loop on amd64, 64-byte NEON loop on arm64) and was not part of go-and's benchmark, so the gap there is unmeasured and likely much smaller than the README's naive-loop ratio.

Fastest possible popcount on x86: amd64 Popcnt is scalar POPCNTQ summed into one register (no AVX2 Harley-Seal or VPSHUFB method); issue #17 asking for the Mula-Kurz-Lemire AVX2 popcount has been open since July 2024.
arm64 users who need Not, Any, AnyMasked or PopcntMasked fast: on arm64 these are pure-Go fallbacks (TODO comments in and_arm64.go).
C/C++ projects: this is a Go package with Go-ABI assembly, not callable from C++ (and maturity is low: 2 stars, no tagged releases).

integration.dependencies: golang.org/x/sys (CPU feature detection); avo only to regenerate the amd64 assembly (separate internal/asm module)
integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.24 (go.mod go 1.24.0; tests use b.Loop); CI runs Go 1.25
integration.platforms: amd64 (AVX2 path, AVX1 fallback, POPCNT path; runtime or GOAMD64-level dispatch), arm64 NEON for And/Or/Xor/AndNot/Popcnt/Memset, pure-Go fallback elsewhere (CI builds 386) or with -tags purego
integration.thread_safety: not documented; functions are stateless and touch only the caller's slices, so concurrent calls on disjoint dst slices are safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces hand-written Go loops one call per loop; vs crypto/subtle.XORBytes the semantics differ (go-and panics on any length mismatch, XORBytes processes min(len(x), len(y)) and returns n)

gotchas: Two-input functions panic unless all slices have equal length; Popcnt, Any and Memset do no length checks. Exact in-place use (dst == a) works and is what the benchmarks do; partially overlapping slices are not documented and the 256-byte block load-then-store order would differ from a byte loop.

Benchmark harness caveats: the headline 15x geomean is against a one-byte-at-a-time loop; against the uint64 purego build it is about 5.1x (i9-13900) and 4.6x (M2 Pro), derived from page data. And/Or/Xor/AndNot/Any rows use 32,000-byte buffers (L1/L2 resident), Popcnt rows 1,000,000 bytes, Any/AnyMasked scan all-zero buffers (worst case), the purego build runs at default GOAMD64 (v2/v3 not measured), the Go version is not printed, and the hybrid i9-13900 run is not pinned to a P-core. No correctness bug found in the measured code: tests compare every SIMD function with the naive loop for sizes 1 to 2^19 plus random tails.

amd64 Popcnt (41.4 GiB/s on the i9-13900) runs at about half the arm64 NEON Popcnt rate (82.4 GiB/s on the M2 Pro); its single-accumulator add chain caps it near 8 bytes per cycle (estimate), so the 2.95x win over purego is from unrolling, not SIMD.

CI (GitHub Actions, ubuntu-latest) runs the tests only on amd64; the arm64 NEON path is only compiled in CI, never executed, and the Apple M2 Pro table dates from August 2024 (it has a Memset row and no Any, AnyMasked or PopcntMasked rows).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick go-and in Go code that needs whole-slice AND/OR/XOR/ANDNOT, any-bit tests or total popcounts; cespare/xxhash is the same asm-versus-purego Go pattern for hashing, and pospop (clausecker) is the better choice when you need positional (per-bit-index) popcounts or AVX-512/AVX2 counting, since go-and's amd64 popcount is scalar POPCNT.
verified_claims_summary: With the repo's benchmark.sh (go test -count=10, benchstat) on an Intel Core i9-13900 under Linux, Go gc with default flags and an unrecorded Go version, And/Or/Xor/AndNot on 32,000-byte buffers took about 361 ns per call versus 6,943 ns for a naive byte loop (19x) and 2,826 ns for the uint64 purego build (7.8x); Popcnt on 1 MB took 22.5 us versus 177.5 us naive and 66.5 us purego (2.95x), for geomeans of 15.4x over naive and 5.1x over purego (derived from page data). An older Apple M2 Pro table (NEON) gives a geomean of 21x over naive and 4.6x over purego (derived from page data).
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-07-26, PRs from three contributors, CI on Go 1.25) and MIT-licensed, small enough to vendor, but it has 2 stars, no tagged releases and an untested arm64 path in CI.
